cohort: The study included 917 consecutive patients with histologically diagnosed endometrial cancer who underwent abdominal, laparoscopic, or robotic hysterectomy between 2008 and 2019.
finding: Minimally invasive surgical approaches (LH and RH) resulted in superior peri-operative outcomes compared to abdominal hysterectomy (AH), with overall survival and disease-free survival for all stages not being significantly influenced by the type of surgical approach, despite some variation in DFS for early-stage EC.
followup_time: Up to 11 years (based on study period 2008-2019 for survival outcomes)
